subject: Clustered self-serve credit issuances — device rotation + disposable domains
messages:
From: fraud-alerts@redwood.ai

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: [Automated] Spike in self-serve credit grants (cluster detected)

Hi team,

Our self-serve credit engine flagged a cluster of ~82 grants in the last 18 hours associated with the domain set *@mailinator.* and *@tempmail.* and a small set of accounts showing rotating device fingerprints and empty billing details. Median session length is 12s, and embedding calls per account are <10 — classic trial probe pattern.

Top-line:
- First detection: 2027-06-20 01:22 UTC
- Impact: 82 trial credits issued (total value estimated ~ $1.2k)
- Signal highlights: disposable domains, device rotation, repeated IP netblocks (AS61903)

I've attached a brief snapshot (signup_snapshot.csv) and a sample of telemetry (device-telemetry-sample.json). Recommend triage for manual rollback and a short freeze on auto-issuance for the affected cohorts.

Stopping auto-credits for impacted cohorts would reduce exposure immediately. Thoughts?

-- Redwood Fraud Detection (automated)

Adding initial HubSpot notes — quick summary from record pulls: ~60% of the flagged emails have no company name, and ~70% have disposable domains. The remaining accounts are generic company names with no usage history. I attached a quick signals PDF so everyone has the same view.

Proposal:
- Temp-disable automated self-serve grants for signups where email domain matches the disposable list OR device-fingerprint reuse > 3 across accounts
- Run a 24-hour manual review window for the 82 accounts, rollback credits for confirmed bots
- Notify affected legitimate users with an appeal form if we retract credits

If Dev can put the throttle in place, we can cut exposure quickly.

[Attachment: fraud-signals-summary.pdf (PDF, 75KB)]

— Marissa

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clustered self-serve credit grants — device rotation + disposable domains

I pushed a conservative throttle on the auto-issuance rule for the matching cohorts at 08:30 PT this morning (ruleset id: auto-credit-v3). New signups that match domain OR device-reuse > 2 are queued for manual review; grants are paused. We added a short 403 path on the API that returns a human-readable reason code when a user is blocked.

I've also opened INF-3421 for the longer-term fix to add a weighted fraud score to issuance logic. Please note: throttling will catch a small number of legitimate signups (estimated ~4-6) — we'll email appeals with a temporary credit hold explanation.

— Dev

Hi Sarah — thanks for reaching out and sorry for the noise. Short answer: those email aliases (e.g., @flux.testmail) match the disposable domain patterns we blocked. We paused auto-issuance this morning and are doing a 24h manual review of the affected accounts.

What we'll do next:
- Rollback credits on accounts confirmed to be created from disposable domains or with matching device fingerprints used across multiple accounts.
- For any legitimate internal users who were blocked, we'll fast-track manual verification and re-issue credits.
- Provide a short incident note you can share with your security and ops teams (I'll attach it when completed).

We estimate the customer impact will be minimal — our throttle is intentionally conservative and we will treat any rollback with an appeal path. I'll follow up with the incident note and a CSV of the specific account IDs we retract.

Apologies again — we're on it.
